subject: Spectral Insight — technical scan, SLOs & next commitments
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@spectralinsight.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Spectral Insight — technical scan, SLOs & next commitments

Hi Ellen / Tom,

Thanks again for your time today. Quick written summary so we have an aligned set of asks and the technical constraints we discussed. Please correct anything I’ve missed.

Key pain points (as discussed)
- User-facing vector search and chat must feel real-time for analysts — target perceived latency at the UI is <200ms for simple retrievals, goal for generation p95 is <=120ms for short prompts.
- High burstiness: nightly enrich jobs plus daytime analyst queries (peak windows 09:00–11:00 and 14:00–16:00 PDT). Need predictable tail-latency during bursts.
- Cost ceiling: rough target for inference cost is <$0.004 per generated response (median length ~150 tokens).
- Data residency & compliance: primary requirement is US-only hosting and SOC 2 + contractual audit support.
- Model needs: mix of a tuned open decoder for retrieval-augmented generation (~30–70B class) plus embeddings model for search; ability to run custom weights is required.

SLO / throughput targets we captured
- Sustained throughput: 1,200 req/s for embed-only traffic (short vectors).
- Mixed load: 600 req/s gen + 2,000 embed ops/s during peak bursts.
- Latency targets: p95 generation <=120ms, p99 <=350ms (goal). Embeddings p95 <=60ms.
- Availability: 99.9% platform SLA, with graceful degradation to a smaller model if the primary is unavailable.

Technical topology (candidate) — initial recommendation
- Dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) in us-west-2 pinned to customer tenancy; 8x GPU nodes (H100-class or equivalent) behind a router that does request-level smart routing.
- KV cache layer (per-tenant, TTL 30m) in front of model replicas for hot prefixes.
- Continuous batching on the serving runtime with latency-aware batching thresholds: max batch window 12ms for generation; dynamic-size batching for embeddings with micro-batches.
- Model variants: primary tuned Llama3-70B quantized to q4/aw4 for throughput; fallback to rwd-instruct-30B-q4 when load/budget constrained. Embeddings: rwd-embed-14b-1.
- Autoscaling policy: maintain 20% headroom above baseline; linear scale up to 2x for 10-minute sustained increases, burst capacity from hosted pool for sudden spikes.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost and latency traces; synthetic prompts for quality regressions.

Action items & next steps
- Redwood (Jonas): produce a capacity sketch and ballpark cost for the topology above — deliverable by Wed, 07 Oct. (I’ll attach a simple MATP spreadsheet.)
- Spectral Insight (Ellen/Tom): share representative prompt/trace samples and a security questionnaire copy (SOC 2) so we can validate data flows.
- Redwood (Neha): draft an architecture diagram (customer-view) and an ops-runbook for the POC. DUE Fri, 09 Oct.
- Schedule: propose a 1-hour hands-on POC kickoff next week (preferred Tue/Wed mornings).

Attachments: I’m attaching a lightweight MATP (SI_SLO_POC_MATP.xlsx) and a Redwood dataplane sketch (redwood-dataplane-architecture.pdf).

If that looks right, I’ll turn the capacity sketch + draft runbook into a short mutual action plan and drop a calendar invite.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spectral Insight — technical scan, SLOs & next commitments

Jonas —

This is perfect, thank you. A few clarifications from our side:
- The p95 120ms target is aggressive but aligns with expectations for the analyst flow — we can relax to 150ms if it keeps costs reasonable; p99 is more important to us for SLA reporting.
- We will need a contract clause guaranteeing US-only processing and a copy of your SOC 2 Type II report (or assessor contact) ahead of any Dedicated deployment.
- For the POC, Tom will share ~50 sample queries and click traces (anonymized) — I’ll send those by EOD Wed.

We’re good for Tue morning next week for the kickoff (10/13 09:00 PDT) if that works for your team.

— Ellen
Ellen Park
VP of Product, Spectral Insight

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Spectral Insight — technical scan, SLOs & next commitments

Quick tech notes for engineering/solutions prep before the kickoff:
- Capacity sketch assumptions:
  • Gen avg tokens per request: 150 tokens (padded headroom 200).
  • Serving efficiency: q4 quantized Llama3-70b -> est 6 tokens/sec/core* on H100-ish runtime (need profiling).
  • KV cache hit-rate target 30–40% for analyst workflows (will reduce tail).
- Queueing & batching: implement latency SLO aware prioritization: short-RTT embedding requests get micro-batched (batch size up to 64, max wait 8ms), gen traffic uses adaptive batching with max window 12ms; cap tokens-per-batch to avoid memory blowouts.
- Observability hooks: add p95/p99 alerts, synthetic prompt evaluation pipeline, and a model-fallback circuit breaker that automatically lowers to 30B variant at 85% CPU/GPU utilization for more than 90s.
- Security/compliance: recommend starting the SOC2 attestation exchange now; Grace, can you pull the standard redwood SOC2 packet & a short note on our US-only tenancy controls?

I’ll draft the runbook and put a first-pass capacity/cost table in the MATP attachment.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
